paper.title_en: Non-classical photon statistics in frequency-modulated double quantum dot cavity systems
paper.abstract_en: The quantum dynamics of a double quantum dot two-level system, coupled to a leaking microwave resonator mode, is theoretically investigated. The double quantum dot is driven by applying a continuous field giving rise to time-dependent modulations of its energy separation between the ground levels of each dot, forming the qubit. Therefore, the cavity resonances occur when the difference between the resonator and the qubit frequencies equals the multiple of the modulation frequency, respectively. In the strong Coulomb interaction limit and the weak couplings of the combined system, i.e. the qubit and the single-mode cavity, to corresponding electronic, phononic or photonic reservoirs, we have demonstrated that the output cavity electromagnetic field is formed of a single-photon flux obeying the sub-Poissonian quantum photon statistics. This was proved via Fano’s factor behaviour or by comparing the resonator’s second- and third-order photon correlation functions, respectively. The phonon, the cavity mode dephasing or the environmental temperatures influence on the quantum properties of the photons are also discussed. •A master equation is derived for a frequency modulated DQD coupled to a cavity mode.•An exact system of equations for our sample is derived, within some approximations.•Single photons with sub-Poissonian statistics are generated in the resonator mode.
